# hearing

Pluggable meeting transcription & context-connected AI agents — batch today, live next.

`hearing` captures, transcribes, and reasons over meeting audio as four small,
**swappable** concerns wired by composition, not baked together:

```default
capture ──audio──▶ STT ──segments──▶ diarization ──labeled──▶ agents
(mic + system,     (local or          (who spoke              (summaries, actions,
 separate channels) cloud, pluggable)  when / "me vs them")     live notes, research)
```

The one-liner just works; everything else is an optional keyword argument.

```python
from hearing import transcribe

transcript = transcribe("meeting.wav")  # -> Transcript (list of segments)
print(transcript.formatted())
```

## Install

```bash
pip install hearing                 # core: data model, channel split, CLI
pip install 'hearing[whisper]'      # + default local STT engine (faster-whisper)
pip install 'hearing[agents]'       # + Claude-backed agent layer
pip install 'hearing[all]'          # whisper + agents + capture + http + storage (dol)
pip install 'hearing[diarize]'      # + pyannote (separate individual remote speakers)
```

### STT engines

One `STTEngine` facade, many engines; pick one with `--engine` (CLI) or `get_engine(name)` (Python). Nothing downstream changes.

| `--engine`          | Engine                                                           | Install             | Needs                                                                         |
|---------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `whisper` (default) | faster-whisper, local, any CPU/GPU                               | `hearing[whisper]`  | —                                                                             |
| `openai`            | OpenAI transcription API (cloud)                                 | `hearing[openai]`   | `OPENAI_API_KEY`                                                              |
| `deepgram`          | Deepgram Nova-3 (cloud; `--model nova-2` etc. swaps it)          | `hearing[deepgram]` | `DEEPGRAM_API_KEY`                                                            |
| `mlx`               | Whisper on Apple Silicon via mlx-whisper                         | `hearing[mlx]`      | macOS on M-series                                                             |
| `parakeet`          | NVIDIA Parakeet-TDT on Apple Silicon via parakeet-mlx            | `hearing[mlx]`      | macOS on M-series, plus `ffmpeg` on PATH (parakeet-mlx decodes audio with it) |
| `whisperx`          | WhisperX: aligned word timestamps, optional pyannote diarization | `hearing[whisperx]` | `HF_TOKEN` (diarization only)                                                 |

The live path (`hearing live`, `stream_transcribe`) works with every engine: engines without native streaming are fed VAD-segmented utterances. `--model` overrides the engine’s default model (a whisper size such as `small` for whisper/mlx/whisperx, a model name for cloud engines).

## What works today (the batch milestone)

Give it a recording and get back a **speaker-labelled transcript** plus optional
**AI meeting notes**. If the file has the mic on one channel and the system audio
(everyone else) on another, you get “me vs them” labelling *for free* — no
diarization model, no voice enrollment — because the channel itself tells you
who is local.

```bash
hearing transcribe meeting.wav                      # diarized transcript to stdout
hearing transcribe meeting.wav --model small --out notes.json
hearing transcribe meeting.wav --engine openai      # cloud STT (OpenAI); needs OPENAI_API_KEY + hearing[openai]
hearing transcribe meeting.wav --engine deepgram    # cloud STT (Deepgram Nova-3); needs DEEPGRAM_API_KEY + hearing[deepgram]
hearing transcribe meeting.wav --engine mlx         # local, Apple Silicon (hearing[mlx]); also: parakeet, whisperx
hearing transcribe meeting.wav --save ./meetings    # persist the transcript (then `hearing meetings ./meetings`)
hearing summarize  meeting.wav                      # transcribe + AI notes (Claude)
hearing summarize  meeting.wav --agent extractive   # offline, no API key needed
hearing summarize  meeting.wav --context-dir ./project_notes   # context-connected: RAG over your docs
hearing summarize  meeting.wav --web-search         # also pull Wikipedia fact context (key-free)
hearing live       meeting.wav                      # STREAM it: finalized segments as utterances complete
hearing meetings   ./meetings                       # list saved transcripts (--show ID to print one)
hearing info                                        # what's installed / available
```

**Context-connected agents.** Point `--context-dir` at a folder of `.md`/`.txt`
notes (prior meetings’ takeaways, project docs); the agent does RAG over them and
brings in facts that aren’t in the transcript (who owns what, prior decisions,
budgets, deadlines). The retriever and a web-search hook are pluggable
Protocols (`hearing/context.py`): `KeywordRetriever` (TF-IDF, dependency-free,
the default) or `EmbeddingRetriever` (OpenAI semantic recall) — choose with
`--retriever keyword|embedding`. Swap in any vector backend behind the same
`Retriever` interface.

### Live / streaming (milestone 2 — core working)

The same pipeline runs as a low-latency loop: VAD finds utterance boundaries,
each finalized utterance is transcribed and emitted as it completes, and the
channel split still labels “me vs them” — the `STTEngine` and agent interfaces
are unchanged from batch.

```python
import asyncio
from hearing import live_transcribe
from hearing.capture import (
    StreamingFileCapture,
)  # or DeviceCapture for a live mic+system device


async def main():
    async for seg in live_transcribe(source=StreamingFileCapture("meeting.wav")):
        print(
            seg.speaker, seg.text
        )  # finalized (seg.meta['final']) segments, as they land


asyncio.run(main())
```

Capturing from a live **device** (`DeviceCapture`, an Aggregate Device with mic

+ BlackHole) is implemented but needs that hardware to verify; streaming a file
  works anywhere.

**Command palette (⌘K).** Press ⌘K (or click the button) for a command palette —
export the transcript (markdown/SRT/JSON), focus search, clear. Each command is
defined once (`frontend/src/commands.ts`, the acture pattern) and also projects to
an AI/MCP tool schema via `toAITools()`, so the same definition can drive the
palette and an AI assistant. Run the frontend’s unit tests with `npm test`.

Example transcript + Claude summary (from `examples/demo_meeting.py`, which
synthesizes a two-speaker meeting with macOS `say` — no mic needed):

```default
[00:00:00] me:   Hi everyone, thanks for joining the planning sync. I'll own the
                 API design and send a draft by Friday. What is our deadline...
[00:00:08] them: Thanks. The launch deadline is the end of the month. Let's
                 decide on the database. I think we should use Postgres...

## Decisions
- PostgreSQL selected as the database for the project.
## Action items
- [me] Own the API design and send a draft by Friday.
## Open questions / follow-ups
- Confirm the exact end-of-month launch deadline.
```

### Composition (dependency injection)

Every concern is a `typing.Protocol`; swap one by changing a single argument.

```python
from hearing import transcribe
from hearing.stt import FasterWhisperSTT
from hearing.diarize import ChannelTrickDiarizer, PyannoteDiarizer
from hearing.agents import ClaudeAgent, ExtractiveAgent

from hearing.stt import OpenAISTT  # or DeepgramSTT, MLXSTT, WhisperXSTT

transcribe(
    "meeting.wav",
    engine=OpenAISTT(),  # cloud STT — one line vs FasterWhisperSTT()
    diarizer=PyannoteDiarizer(),  # upgrade from the channel trick
    agent=ClaudeAgent(context="prior meeting takeaways..."),  # or ExtractiveAgent()
)
```

The shared data spine is `hearing.types.TranscriptSegment` — a frozen, standoff
interval annotation (time is **integer milliseconds**, never float). See
`hearing/interfaces.py` for the four facade Protocols (`CaptureSource`,
`STTEngine`, `Diarizer`, `AgentConsumer`).

## Capturing the audio (macOS)

`hearing` reads multi-channel audio files and splits the channels. To get a
recording with mic on one channel and system audio (the other participants) on
another, use **BlackHole + an Aggregate Device** or **Core Audio taps** — the
mechanics, the channel layout, and the iOS limits are documented in the
`hearing-audio-capture` agent skill (`.claude/skills/hearing-audio-capture/`).
Live device capture is the next milestone; today you bring a recording.

## Not yet (designed, on the roadmap)

- **Native streaming engines** (Deepgram websocket, OpenAI Realtime,
  WhisperLive) behind the same `STTEngine` facade — today every engine streams
  through VAD-segmented batch calls — and **semantic turn detection** — see
  `hearing-live-pipeline`.
- **Live device capture verified on hardware** (`DeviceCapture` is written; needs
  a BlackHole + Aggregate Device) — see `hearing-audio-capture`.
- **TypeScript frontend** (schema-driven transcript viewer + copilot overlay
  with zodal/acture) — see `hearing-frontend`.

Full status in [`misc/docs/ROADMAP.md`]().

## Web UI (HTTP API + React frontend)

A FastAPI layer wraps the same facades, and a schema-driven React frontend
(zodal + Zod) renders the diarized transcript (me/them lanes) and the AI notes.

```bash
pip install 'hearing[http,whisper,agents]'
hearing serve                      # API on http://127.0.0.1:8000 (docs at /docs)

cd frontend && npm install && npm run dev   # UI on http://localhost:5173 (proxies /api)
```

Then drop an audio file on the page → diarized transcript + AI meeting notes.
Tick **Live stream** to watch finalized segments append in real time as the live
pipeline produces them (`POST /api/transcribe/stream`, NDJSON). The
TypeScript data shapes live in `frontend/src/schema.ts` as zodal collections
(one Zod schema per surface) and double as the API response validator, so the
Python backend and the UI share one contract. See the `hearing-frontend` skill.

## Architecture & development

This project is developed with a suite of agent **skills** under
`.claude/skills/` — start with the `hearing` skill (the project-manager /
orchestrator), which routes to the per-concern skills (`hearing-architecture`,
`hearing-audio-capture`, `hearing-stt`, `hearing-diarization`, `hearing-agents`,
`hearing-live-pipeline`, `hearing-frontend`). The two research reports the design
is grounded in are in `misc/docs/`.

# _autosummary/hearing.agents.html.md

# hearing.agents

The agent / “copilot” layer — the actual point of the hearing project.

An agent consumes a (speaker-labelled) transcript and produces feedback. The
*same* [`AgentConsumer`](_autosummary/hearing.interfaces.html.md#hearing.interfaces.AgentConsumer) interface serves both modes;
only *when* and *what granularity* it consumes differs:

* **batch** — `on_window(whole_transcript)` -> summary, action items,
  decisions, open questions, follow-up research (post-meeting).
* **live** — `on_segment(finalized_segment)` -> running notes, suggested
  questions, surfaced docs, fact-checks (as the meeting unfolds).

Agents are meant to be *context-connected*: bound to a meeting/project and able
to draw on accumulated knowledge (prior takeaways, the codebase, research
reports) and live web search. The `context` field is that hook.

The default backend is Claude (latest/most capable) but stays pluggable — see
the `claude-api` skill for model ids, pricing, tool use, and structured
output, and the `hearing-agents` skill for the queue-consumer pattern, RAG,
and the batch≡live unification.

Pick the best available agent.

`prefer="claude"` forces Claude; `"extractive"` forces the offline
fallback; `"auto"` (default) uses Claude when the anthropic SDK and an API
key are available, otherwise the dependency-free [`ExtractiveAgent`](_autosummary/hearing.agents.html.md#hearing.agents.ExtractiveAgent).
A `retriever`/`web_search` make the Claude agent context-connected.

# _autosummary/hearing.backends.html.md

# hearing.backends

Extra scribed backends that hearing contributes: Apple-Silicon MLX and WhisperX.

hearing’s STT runs through scribed (see [`hearing.stt`](_autosummary/hearing.stt.html.md#module-hearing.stt)). scribed already ships
the cloud engines (OpenAI, Deepgram, AssemblyAI, …) and faster-whisper; the
engines below are not in scribed yet, so hearing provides them as \*\*scribed
plugins\*\*, registered at runtime with `scribed.register_backend()`:

- `mlx-whisper` — Whisper on Apple Silicon via MLX (`pip install 'hearing[mlx]'`)
- `parakeet-mlx` — NVIDIA Parakeet-TDT on Apple Silicon via MLX (same extra)
- `whisperx` — WhisperX: batched Whisper + word alignment + optional pyannote
  diarization (`pip install 'hearing[whisperx]'`)

Each backend is a subpackage laid out exactly like a `scribed.backends.<id>`
package (`config.py` with `BACKEND_CONFIG`, `adapter.py` with `Adapter`),
so it can move into scribed verbatim. Registration is lazy and non-clobbering:
[`register_backends()`](_autosummary/hearing.backends.html.md#hearing.backends.register_backends) only adds an id scribed does not already provide, so
once scribed ships one of these, scribed’s own implementation wins.

Nothing here imports an engine SDK at import time; the adapters import it on first
transcription and raise an informative error (naming the extra) when it is absent,
or — for the MLX engines — when not running on Apple Silicon.

### hearing.backends.register_backends(backend_ids=None, , registry=None)

Register hearing’s backends with scribed’s registry; return the ids added.

Idempotent and non-clobbering: an id scribed already knows is left alone.
The adapter itself is loaded lazily by scribed (from `module_path`).

* **Parameters:**
  * **backend_ids** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Iterable)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]) – which backends to register (default: all of them).
  * **registry** ([`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)) – the scribed registry module (injectable for tests).
* **Return type:**
  [`List`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.List)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

Raise an informative `RuntimeError` unless running on Apple Silicon.

  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### hearing.backends.require_module(module_name, , engine, extra)

Import `module_name` or raise an `ImportError` that names the extra.

* **Return type:**
  [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)

### hearing.backends.to_waveform_16k(audio)

Decode any scribed audio input to a float32 mono 16 kHz numpy array.

Whisper-family engines accept such an array directly, which avoids their
ffmpeg-based file loading (hearing hands utterances over as WAV bytes).

* **Return type:**
  [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)

### hearing.backends.whisper_result_to_segments(result)

Build scribed `Segment`s from an openai-whisper-style result dict.

Handles both mlx-whisper (word `probability`) and WhisperX (word `score`,
optional `speaker` on segments and words). Times are float seconds.

```pycon
>>> segs = whisper_result_to_segments({"segments": [
...     {"start": 0.0, "end": 1.5, "text": " hi there",
...      "words": [{"word": " hi", "start": 0.0, "end": 0.4, "probability": 0.9}]}
... ]})
>>> segs[0].text, segs[0].span.end_ms, segs[0].words[0].text
('hi there', 1500, 'hi')
```

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)

# _autosummary/hearing.backends.mlx_whisper.adapter.html.md

# hearing.backends.mlx_whisper.adapter

Adapter for the mlx-whisper backend (Whisper on Apple Silicon via MLX).

Decodes the input to a float32 mono 16 kHz array (no ffmpeg needed), calls
`mlx_whisper.transcribe(array, path_or_hf_repo=...)` and maps its
openai-whisper-shaped result dict onto a `scribed.base.Transcript`.
`mlx_whisper` is imported on first use, after the Apple-Silicon check, so this

# _autosummary/hearing.backends.mlx_whisper.config.html.md

# hearing.backends.mlx_whisper.config

Configuration for the mlx-whisper backend (Whisper on Apple Silicon via MLX).

[mlx-whisper](https://pypi.org/project/mlx-whisper/) is Apple’s (ml-explore)
port of OpenAI Whisper to MLX: it runs on the M-series GPU with unified memory, and
returns openai-whisper-shaped results (segments, optional word timestamps).
macOS on Apple Silicon only.

`model` is either a Hugging Face repo id (`"mlx-community/whisper-large-v3-turbo"`,
the default) or a bare Whisper size (`"tiny"`, `"base"`, `"small"`,
`"medium"`, `"large-v3"`, `"turbo"`), resolved by
[`hearing.backends.mlx_whisper.adapter.resolve_model_repo()`](_autosummary/hearing.backends.mlx_whisper.adapter.html.md#hearing.backends.mlx_whisper.adapter.resolve_model_repo).

### Module Attributes

| [`DEFAULT_MODEL`](_autosummary/hearing.backends.mlx_whisper.config.html.md#hearing.backends.mlx_whisper.config.DEFAULT_MODEL)   | Default MLX Whisper weights (fast and accurate on M2+).   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------|

### hearing.backends.mlx_whisper.config.DEFAULT_MODEL *= 'mlx-community/whisper-large-v3-turbo'*

Default MLX Whisper weights (fast and accurate on M2+).

# hearing.backends.parakeet_mlx.adapter

Adapter for the parakeet-mlx backend (NVIDIA Parakeet-TDT on Apple Silicon).

Loads a model with `parakeet_mlx.from_pretrained(repo)` (cached per repo),
transcribes a temporary audio file, and maps the returned `AlignedResult`’s
sentences (text + float-second `start`/`end`) onto scribed segments.
Parakeet’s tokens are sub-word pieces, so no word list is emitted.
`parakeet_mlx` is imported on first use, after the Apple-Silicon check.

# _autosummary/hearing.backends.whisperx.adapter.html.md

# hearing.backends.whisperx.adapter

Adapter for the WhisperX backend (transcribe -> align -> optionally diarize).

Pipeline, on a float32 mono 16 kHz array (no ffmpeg needed):

1. `whisperx.load_model(model, device, compute_type=...)` (cached) then
   `.transcribe(audio, batch_size=..., language=...)`;
2. if `align`: `whisperx.load_align_model` + `whisperx.align` for accurate
   word timestamps;
3. if `diarize`: pyannote via WhisperX’s `DiarizationPipeline` +
   `whisperx.assign_word_speakers` (needs a Hugging Face token, env `HF_TOKEN`).

The result is openai-whisper-shaped, mapped by
[`hearing.backends.whisper_result_to_segments()`](_autosummary/hearing.backends.html.md#hearing.backends.whisper_result_to_segments). `whisperx` (and `torch`,
for device auto-detection) are imported on first use.

### Module Attributes

| [`DEFAULT_COMPUTE_TYPES`](_autosummary/hearing.backends.whisperx.adapter.html.md#hearing.backends.whisperx.adapter.DEFAULT_COMPUTE_TYPES)   | `compute_type` used when none is given, by device.   |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------|

### Classes

| [`Adapter`](_autosummary/hearing.backends.whisperx.adapter.html.md#hearing.backends.whisperx.adapter.Adapter)(config)   | WhisperX adapter (caches ASR, alignment and diarization models).   |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|

### *class* hearing.backends.whisperx.adapter.Adapter(config)

Bases: `BaseTranscriberAdapter`

WhisperX adapter (caches ASR, alignment and diarization models).

#### module_name *= 'whisperx'*

Engine module name — the seam tests use to inject a fake backend.

### hearing.backends.whisperx.adapter.DEFAULT_COMPUTE_TYPES *= {'cpu': 'int8', 'cuda': 'float16'}*

`compute_type` used when none is given, by device.


# _autosummary/hearing.backends.whisperx.config.html.md

# hearing.backends.whisperx.config

Configuration for the WhisperX backend.

[WhisperX](https://github.com/m-bain/whisperX) = batched faster-whisper +
wav2vec2 forced alignment (accurate word timestamps) + optional pyannote speaker
diarization, in one pass — the sweet spot for multi-speaker meetings.

Diarization is off by default (in hearing, speakers are a separate concern — see
the `hearing-diarization` skill); pass `diarize=True` to have WhisperX label
speakers. It needs a Hugging Face token (env `HF_TOKEN`) that has accepted the
pyannote model terms. `device`/`compute_type` default to CUDA + float16 when a
GPU is visible, else CPU + int8.

### Module Attributes

| [`DEFAULT_MODEL`](_autosummary/hearing.backends.whisperx.config.html.md#hearing.backends.whisperx.config.DEFAULT_MODEL)     | Default Whisper model size for WhisperX.                              |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`HF_TOKEN_ENV_VARS`](_autosummary/hearing.backends.whisperx.config.html.md#hearing.backends.whisperx.config.HF_TOKEN_ENV_VARS) | Env var(s) holding the Hugging Face token pyannote diarization needs. |

### hearing.backends.whisperx.config.DEFAULT_MODEL *= 'large-v3'*

Default Whisper model size for WhisperX.

### hearing.backends.whisperx.config.HF_TOKEN_ENV_VARS *= ('HF_TOKEN', 'HUGGING_FACE_HUB_TOKEN')*

Env var(s) holding the Hugging Face token pyannote diarization needs.

# _autosummary/hearing.capture.html.md

# hearing.capture

Audio capture and channel handling for the hearing pipeline.

This module owns turning an audio *source* into per-channel float arrays, and the
all-important **channel split**: mic and system audio are kept on separate channels
so that “who is local” is known for free (see the `hearing-diarization` skill for
what we do with that, and `hearing-audio-capture` for the macOS mechanics —
BlackHole + Aggregate Device, or Core Audio taps).

The generic, channel-agnostic conditioning (decode, down-mix, resample, energy) now
lives in `scribed.audio` and is re-exported here for backward compatibility —
hearing owns only the multi-channel / “me vs them” concerns.

### Functions

| [`split_channels`](_autosummary/hearing.capture.html.md#hearing.capture.split_channels)(data, \*[, mic_channels, ...])   | Split a multi-channel array into per-`Channel` mono arrays.   |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|

### Classes

| [`ChannelSplitFileCapture`](_autosummary/hearing.capture.html.md#hearing.capture.ChannelSplitFileCapture)(path[, ...])        | A batch [`CaptureSource`](_autosummary/hearing.interfaces.html.md#hearing.interfaces.CaptureSource) over an audio file.   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`DeviceCapture`](_autosummary/hearing.capture.html.md#hearing.capture.DeviceCapture)([device, block_ms, ...])      | Live macOS capture from an audio *device* (the milestone-2 capture source).                                                   |
| [`StreamingFileCapture`](_autosummary/hearing.capture.html.md#hearing.capture.StreamingFileCapture)(path[, block_ms, ...]) | A *streaming* [`CaptureSource`](_autosummary/hearing.interfaces.html.md#hearing.interfaces.CaptureSource) over a file.    |

### *class* hearing.capture.ChannelSplitFileCapture(path, mic_channels=(0,), system_channels=(1,))

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A batch [`CaptureSource`](_autosummary/hearing.interfaces.html.md#hearing.interfaces.CaptureSource) over an audio file.

Reads the file once and yields `(channel, mono_frames)` for each channel
present. The live counterpart (device/tap) implements the same interface;
swapping it in is the *only* change needed to go live — see the
`hearing-live-pipeline` skill.

Typical use (needs a real audio file, so it is not run as a doctest):

```default
ChannelSplitFileCapture("meeting.wav").frames()
```

#### *async* astream()

Stream the file’s channels in one shot (whole clip per channel).

Provided so a file satisfies the async `CaptureSource` too; for a
realistic block-by-block live simulation use [`StreamingFileCapture`](_autosummary/hearing.capture.html.md#hearing.capture.StreamingFileCapture).

* **Return type:**
  [`AsyncIterator`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.AsyncIterator)[[`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`Channel`](_autosummary/hearing.types.html.md#hearing.types.Channel), `ndarray`]]

#### channels()

The per-channel mono arrays at the file’s native sample rate.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`Channel`](_autosummary/hearing.types.html.md#hearing.types.Channel), `ndarray`]

#### frames()

Yield `(channel, mono_frames)` once per channel (whole clip).

* **Return type:**
  [`Iterator`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Iterator)[[`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`Channel`](_autosummary/hearing.types.html.md#hearing.types.Channel), `ndarray`]]

### *class* hearing.capture.DeviceCapture(device=None, block_ms=200, mic_channels=(0, 1), system_channels=(2, 3), sample_rate=48000, channels_count=4)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Live macOS capture from an audio *device* (the milestone-2 capture source).

Point this at an **Aggregate Device** that combines your microphone and
BlackHole (so mic and system audio land on separate, non-mixed channels —
see the `hearing-audio-capture` skill for the Audio MIDI Setup). Reads
multi-channel blocks and splits them into mic/system channels.

Requires `pip install 'hearing[capture]'` (sounddevice). Needs real audio
hardware to exercise; constructing it is cheap (the device opens in
`astream`). For a hardware-free run of the live loop, use
[`StreamingFileCapture`](_autosummary/hearing.capture.html.md#hearing.capture.StreamingFileCapture).

#### *async* astream()

Open the device and yield `(channel, block)` blocks until cancelled.

* **Return type:**
  [`AsyncIterator`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.AsyncIterator)[[`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`Channel`](_autosummary/hearing.types.html.md#hearing.types.Channel), `ndarray`]]

#### *static* list_devices()

Return available audio devices (helps pick the Aggregate Device).

### *class* hearing.capture.StreamingFileCapture(path, block_ms=200, realtime=False, mic_channels=(0,), system_channels=(1,))

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A *streaming* [`CaptureSource`](_autosummary/hearing.interfaces.html.md#hearing.interfaces.CaptureSource) over a file.

Yields `(channel, block)` in `block_ms` chunks, time-ordered across
channels, so the live pipeline can be exercised end-to-end without a mic or
BlackHole. With `realtime=True` it paces playback in real time (for demos);
the default streams as fast as possible (for tests).

#### *async* astream()

Yield `(channel, block)` blocks, all channels per time step.

* **Return type:**
  [`AsyncIterator`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.AsyncIterator)[[`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`Channel`](_autosummary/hearing.types.html.md#hearing.types.Channel), `ndarray`]]

#### channels()

The per-channel mono arrays at the file’s native sample rate.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`Channel`](_autosummary/hearing.types.html.md#hearing.types.Channel), `ndarray`]

#### frames()

Batch view: whole clip per channel.

* **Return type:**
  [`Iterator`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Iterator)[[`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`Channel`](_autosummary/hearing.types.html.md#hearing.types.Channel), `ndarray`]]

### hearing.capture.split_channels(data, , mic_channels=(0,), system_channels=(1,))

Split a multi-channel array into per-`Channel` mono arrays.

An aggregate device *does not mix* — mic lands on one set of channels and
system audio on another — so we can slice the columns apart. A mono file
(or single-column) has no split; it is returned as `{Channel.MIXED: ...}`.

* **Parameters:**
  * **data** (`ndarray`) – shape `(n_samples,)` or `(n_samples, n_channels)`.
  * **mic_channels** ([`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]) – column indices carrying the local microphone.
  * **system_channels** ([`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]) – column indices carrying captured system audio.
* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`Channel`](_autosummary/hearing.types.html.md#hearing.types.Channel), `ndarray`]
* **Returns:**
  Mapping from `Channel` to a mono float32 array. Channels whose
  indices are out of range are silently omitted.


# _autosummary/hearing.cli.html.md

# hearing.cli

Command-line interface for hearing, dispatched with `cw`.

Surfaces the Python facades (`transcribe`, `summarize`) as subcommands — it does
not reimplement them (the facades are the SSOT; see the `python-dispatching`
and `hearing-architecture` skills). Installed as the `hearing` console
script:

```default
hearing transcribe meeting.wav
hearing transcribe meeting.wav --model small --out notes.json
hearing transcribe meeting.wav --engine deepgram   # or openai / mlx / parakeet / whisperx
hearing summarize meeting.wav            # transcribe + AI meeting notes
hearing info                             # check what's installed/available
```

### Functions

| [`info`](_autosummary/hearing.cli.html.md#hearing.cli.info)()                                            | Report which optional components are installed and what's missing.         |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`live`](_autosummary/hearing.cli.html.md#hearing.cli.live)([path, engine, model, device, ...])          | Run the LIVE streaming pipeline, printing segments as utterances finalize. |
| [`main`](_autosummary/hearing.cli.html.md#hearing.cli.main)([argv])                                      | Entry point for the `hearing` console script.                              |
| [`meetings`](_autosummary/hearing.cli.html.md#hearing.cli.meetings)(store, \*[, show])                       | List transcripts saved in a store (or print one with --show ID).           |
| [`serve`](_autosummary/hearing.cli.html.md#hearing.cli.serve)(\*[, host, port, reload])                   | Serve the HTTP API (FastAPI) the frontend talks to.                        |
| [`summarize`](_autosummary/hearing.cli.html.md#hearing.cli.summarize)(path, \*[, agent, model, context, ...]) | Transcribe a meeting and produce AI notes (summary, actions, questions).   |
| [`transcribe`](_autosummary/hearing.cli.html.md#hearing.cli.transcribe)(path, \*[, engine, model, ...])        | Transcribe an audio file to text or JSON.                                  |

### hearing.cli.info()

Report which optional components are installed and what’s missing.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### hearing.cli.live(path=None, , engine='whisper', model=None, device=None, block_ms=200, realtime=False)

Run the LIVE streaming pipeline, printing segments as utterances finalize.

* **Parameters:**
  * **path** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – stream this audio FILE through the live loop (great for a demo /
    no hardware). Omit to capture from an audio DEVICE instead.
  * **engine** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – STT engine (same choices as `transcribe --engine`); engines
    without native streaming are fed VAD-segmented utterances.
  * **model** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – STT model override (omit for the engine’s default).
  * **device** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – audio device index/name for live capture (an Aggregate Device
    with mic + BlackHole; see the hearing-audio-capture skill).
  * **block_ms** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – streaming block size in milliseconds.
  * **realtime** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – when streaming a file, pace it in real time (else as-fast-as).
* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### hearing.cli.main(argv=None)

Entry point for the `hearing` console script.

`cw.run` *returns* the exit code (argh’s `parser.dispatch` exited by
itself), so the `SystemExit` here is what makes `hearing no-such-command`
exit 2.

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### hearing.cli.meetings(store, , show=None)

List transcripts saved in a store (or print one with –show ID).

* **Parameters:**
  * **store** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – the store/folder a transcript was saved to (`transcribe --save`).
  * **show** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – a meeting id to print (formatted transcript) instead of listing.
* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### hearing.cli.serve(, host='127.0.0.1', port=8000, reload=False)

Serve the HTTP API (FastAPI) the frontend talks to.

* **Parameters:**
  * **host** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – bind address.
  * **port** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – bind port.
  * **reload** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – auto-reload on code changes (dev).
* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### hearing.cli.summarize(path, , agent='auto', model=None, context=None, context_dir=None, retriever='keyword', web_search=False, engine='whisper', transcribe_model=None, split=True)

Transcribe a meeting and produce AI notes (summary, actions, questions).

* **Parameters:**
  * **path** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – audio file to transcribe and analyze.
  * **agent** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – “auto” (Claude if available, else offline extractive), “claude”,
    or “extractive” (deterministic, no API key needed).
  * **model** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – Claude model id (only used by the claude/auto agent).
  * **context** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – optional literal context string to connect the agent.
  * **context_dir** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – a folder/file of .txt/.md context docs (prior takeaways,
    project notes); the agent does RAG over it (context-connected).
  * **retriever** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – “keyword” (TF-IDF, offline) or “embedding” (OpenAI semantic;
    needs hearing[openai] + OPENAI_API_KEY). Only used with context_dir.
  * **web_search** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – also bring in Wikipedia fact context (key-free) for the agent.
  * **engine** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – STT engine (same choices as `transcribe --engine`).
  * **transcribe_model** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – STT model override (omit for the engine’s default).
  * **split** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – split mic/system channels (me vs them).
* **Return type:**
  [`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### hearing.cli.transcribe(path, , engine='whisper', model=None, language=None, split=True, diarize=True, out=None, fmt='text', save=None)

Transcribe an audio file to text or JSON.

* **Parameters:**
  * **path** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – audio file (wav/flac/aiff/…; convert mp3/m4a with ffmpeg first).
  * **engine** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – STT engine — “whisper” (local faster-whisper, default), “openai”
    (cloud), “deepgram” (cloud, Nova-3), “mlx” (Whisper on Apple Silicon),
    “parakeet” (Parakeet-TDT on Apple Silicon), or “whisperx” (aligned words).
  * **model** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – engine model override — a whisper size (tiny/base/small/large-v3/…)
    for whisper/mlx/whisperx, a model name for cloud engines (e.g.
    “nova-3”); omit for the engine’s default.
  * **language** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – force a language code (e.g. “en”); omit to auto-detect.
  * **split** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – split mic/system channels for multi-channel files (me vs them).
  * **diarize** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – apply the channel-trick “me vs them” labelling.
  * **out** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – write to this path (.json -> JSON, else formatted text); else stdout.
  * **fmt** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – stdout/text format — “text” or “json”.
  * **save** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – persist the transcript to this store/folder (keyed by the file stem),
    so post-meeting agents can load the full transcript later.
* **Return type:**
  [`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]


# _autosummary/hearing.context.html.md

# hearing.context

Context stores and retrieval (RAG) for context-connected agents.

An agent with no context is just a chatbot — the point of `hearing` is agents
*bound to a meeting and a project*, drawing on accumulated knowledge (prior
takeaways, the codebase, research reports). This module provides the retrieval
side behind a tiny [`Retriever`](_autosummary/hearing.context.html.md#hearing.context.Retriever) Protocol so the backend is swappable and
testable with a fake (per the `hearing-agents` skill).

The default [`KeywordRetriever`](_autosummary/hearing.context.html.md#hearing.context.KeywordRetriever) is a dependency-free TF-IDF retriever —
good enough to wire context-connection end-to-end and fully deterministic for
tests. Swap in an embedding/vector backend (Qdrant + LlamaIndex, or the user’s
own local store — check `my-packages` / `python-storage`) behind the same
Protocol when you need semantic recall.

### Module Attributes

| [`EmbedFn`](_autosummary/hearing.context.html.md#hearing.context.EmbedFn)   | maps texts to equal-length float vectors.   |
|------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------|

### Functions

| [`build_embedding_retriever`](_autosummary/hearing.context.html.md#hearing.context.build_embedding_retriever)(source, \*[, embed])   | Build an [`EmbeddingRetriever`](_autosummary/hearing.context.html.md#hearing.context.EmbeddingRetriever) (default embedder: OpenAI) from a dict, a list, or a folder of `.md`/`.txt` docs (same source forms as [`build_retriever()`](_autosummary/hearing.context.html.md#hearing.context.build_retriever)).   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`build_retriever`](_autosummary/hearing.context.html.md#hearing.context.build_retriever)(source)                          | Build a [`KeywordRetriever`](_autosummary/hearing.context.html.md#hearing.context.KeywordRetriever) from a dict, a list, or a folder/file.                                                                                                                                           |
| [`openai_embedder`](_autosummary/hearing.context.html.md#hearing.context.openai_embedder)(\*[, model, api_key, client])    | Return an [`EmbedFn`](_autosummary/hearing.context.html.md#hearing.context.EmbedFn) backed by the OpenAI embeddings API.                                                                                                                                                    |

sync or async.

### *class* hearing.context.Chunk(text, title='', source='', score=0.0)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A retrieved piece of context: the text plus where it came from.

### hearing.context.EmbedFn

maps texts to equal-length float vectors.

* **Type:**
  A batch embedder

alias of `Callable`[[[`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]], [`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)]]]

### *class* hearing.context.EmbeddingRetriever(docs, , embed)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Semantic retriever: ranks chunks by cosine similarity of embeddings.

The corpus is embedded once at construction; `search` embeds the query and
returns the nearest chunks. The embedder is injected (`embed=`) so it is
backend-agnostic and testable with a deterministic fake — use
[`openai_embedder()`](_autosummary/hearing.context.html.md#hearing.context.openai_embedder) for real semantic recall.

```pycon
>>> import asyncio
>>> fake = lambda texts: [[t.lower().count("db"), t.lower().count("ui")] for t in texts]
>>> r = EmbeddingRetriever({"a": "db db", "b": "ui ui"}, embed=fake)
>>> asyncio.run(r.search("db"))[0].title
'a'
```

#### *async* search(query, , k=4)

Return the top-`k` chunks by cosine similarity to `query`.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Chunk`](_autosummary/hearing.context.html.md#hearing.context.Chunk)]

### *class* hearing.context.KeywordRetriever(docs)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Dependency-free TF-IDF retriever over a small in-memory corpus.

```pycon
>>> import asyncio
>>> r = KeywordRetriever({"db": "We will use PostgreSQL.", "ui": "React frontend."})
>>> hits = asyncio.run(r.search("postgresql migration"))
>>> hits[0].title
'db'
```

Matching is purely lexical, so a query sharing no token with the corpus
retrieves nothing — use [`EmbeddingRetriever`](_autosummary/hearing.context.html.md#hearing.context.EmbeddingRetriever) for semantic recall.

```pycon
>>> asyncio.run(r.search("which database?"))
[]
```

#### *async* search(query, , k=4)

Return the top-`k` chunks by TF-IDF overlap with `query`.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`Chunk`](_autosummary/hearing.context.html.md#hearing.context.Chunk)]

### *class* hearing.context.Retriever(\*args, \*\*kwargs)

Bases: [`Protocol`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Protocol)

Retrieves project/meeting context relevant to a query (RAG).

#### *async* search(query, , k=4)

Return up to `k` chunks most relevant to `query`.

* **Return type:**
  [`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[`Chunk`](_autosummary/hearing.context.html.md#hearing.context.Chunk)]

Bases: [`Protocol`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Protocol)

Brings outside information in — one targeted query, `k` results.

  [`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[`Chunk`](_autosummary/hearing.context.html.md#hearing.context.Chunk)]

### *class* hearing.context.WikipediaSearch(lang='en', timeout=8.0, fetch=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Key-free, dependency-free [`WebSearch`](_autosummary/hearing.context.html.md#hearing.context.WebSearch) over Wikipedia (stdlib urllib).

Ideal for the live fact-check / “who is X / what is Y” use: one targeted
query, a few result snippets with source URLs. The HTTP `fetch` is

# _autosummary/hearing.diarize.html.md

# hearing.diarize

Diarization and speaker labelling for the hearing pipeline.

Two ideas, one interface ([`Diarizer`](_autosummary/hearing.interfaces.html.md#hearing.interfaces.Diarizer)):

1. **The channel trick (default, free).** Because capture keeps the mic and the
   system audio on *separate channels*, we already know who is local: the
   `MIC` channel is “me”, the `SYSTEM` channel is the remote participants.
   [`ChannelTrickDiarizer`](_autosummary/hearing.diarize.html.md#hearing.diarize.ChannelTrickDiarizer) just maps channel -> speaker. No model, no
   > audio, no error from overlap on the local side. This beats voice
   > fingerprinting for the “is it me?” question.
2. **Real diarization (the upgrade).** To separate *multiple remote* speakers
   you need acoustic diarization. [`PyannoteDiarizer`](_autosummary/hearing.diarize.html.md#hearing.diarize.PyannoteDiarizer) wraps
   `pyannote.audio` and runs only on the system channel. A diarized transcript
   is standoff interval annotation with a speaker tier — see the
   `annotation-systems` skill.

See the `hearing-diarization` skill for the full landscape (pyannote vs NeMo
vs WhisperX vs SpeechBrain, DER numbers, enrollment).

### Classes

| [`ChannelTrickDiarizer`](_autosummary/hearing.diarize.html.md#hearing.diarize.ChannelTrickDiarizer)([me_label, them_label])   | Label speakers from the capture channel — the free, reliable default.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`PyannoteDiarizer`](_autosummary/hearing.diarize.html.md#hearing.diarize.PyannoteDiarizer)([model, hf_token, ...])       | Acoustic diarization via `pyannote.audio` (the upgrade path).           |

### *class* hearing.diarize.ChannelTrickDiarizer(me_label='me', them_label='them')

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Label speakers from the capture channel — the free, reliable default.

`MIC` -> `me_label` (the local user), `SYSTEM` -> `them_label` (a
remote participant). Segments already carrying a speaker, or coming from a
`MIXED` channel, are passed through unchanged (there is nothing to infer).

This is the architecture’s default diarizer whenever channel information is
present. To distinguish *individual* remote speakers, compose this with (or
replace it by) [`PyannoteDiarizer`](_autosummary/hearing.diarize.html.md#hearing.diarize.PyannoteDiarizer).

#### assign_speakers(segments, , audio=None, sample_rate=None)

Yield segments with `.speaker` set from their `.channel`.

* **Return type:**
  [`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Iterable)[[`TranscriptSegment`](_autosummary/hearing.types.html.md#hearing.types.TranscriptSegment)]

### *class* hearing.diarize.PyannoteDiarizer(model='pyannote/speaker-diarization-3.1', hf_token=None, speaker_prefix='spk_', me_label='me', pipeline=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Acoustic diarization via `pyannote.audio` (the upgrade path).

Runs the pretrained pipeline over the audio, then assigns each segment the
speaker whose diarized turn overlaps it most. It runs on the *system* channel
only: `MIC` segments are labelled `me_label` for free (the channel trick),
and the model is not run at all when there is nothing left to diarize. Pass
the system-channel audio as `audio` (`transcribe` does).

Requires `pip install hearing[diarize]` and a Hugging Face token with the
pyannote model licenses accepted. The import is guarded so the package works
without it. `pipeline` is the seam: any callable
`({"waveform", "sample_rate"}) -> annotation` (an object with
`itertracks(yield_label=True)`) replaces the pretrained model, which is how
this is tested without a model or a token.

#### assign_speakers(segments, , audio=None, sample_rate=None)

Yield segments labelled: mic -> me, others -> most-overlapping diarized speaker.

* **Return type:**
  [`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Iterable)[[`TranscriptSegment`](_autosummary/hearing.types.html.md#hearing.types.TranscriptSegment)]


# _autosummary/hearing.html.md

# hearing

hearing — pluggable meeting transcription & context-aware AI agents.

A small, composable toolkit for capturing, transcribing, and reasoning over
meeting audio. Four swappable concerns compose into one pipeline by dependency
injection: audio **capture** (mic + system audio on separate channels) ->
**STT** engine facade (local or cloud) -> optional **diarization** / speaker-id
(the mic-vs-system channel split gives “me vs them” for free) -> an **agent**
layer that consumes the transcript (batch or live).

Progressive disclosure — the one-liner just works:

```default
from hearing import transcribe
transcript = transcribe("meeting.wav")
print(transcript.formatted())
```

…while engine selection, diarization, agents, channel routing, and the live
loop are all optional keyword-only arguments.

The architecture and the per-concern guidance live in the project’s agent skills
(`.claude/skills/hearing*`); start with the `hearing` skill.

### Functions

| [`transcribe`](_autosummary/hearing.html.md#hearing.transcribe)(source, \*[, engine, diarizer, ...])   | Transcribe an audio source to a [`Transcript`](_autosummary/hearing.types.html.md#hearing.types.Transcript).   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`live_transcribe`](_autosummary/hearing.html.md#hearing.live_transcribe)(\*, source[, engine, ...])        | Stream FINALIZED segments as a meeting unfolds (the live path).                                                         |
| [`summarize`](_autosummary/hearing.html.md#hearing.summarize)(source, \*[, agent, context, model])    | Transcribe (if needed) then run an agent to produce meeting notes.                                                      |

### Classes

| [`Transcript`](_autosummary/hearing.html.md#hearing.Transcript)([segments, sample_rate, meta])     | A finished transcript: an ordered collection of segments plus metadata.   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`TranscriptSegment`](_autosummary/hearing.html.md#hearing.TranscriptSegment)(text, span[, channel, ...]) | The data spine — a standoff interval annotation over the audio.           |
| [`TimeSpan`](_autosummary/hearing.html.md#hearing.TimeSpan)(start_ms, end_ms)                    | A half-open interval `[start_ms, end_ms)` in integer milliseconds.        |
| [`Word`](_autosummary/hearing.html.md#hearing.Word)(text, span[, confidence])                | Optional word-level timing (WhisperX / `word_timestamps=True`).           |
| [`Channel`](_autosummary/hearing.html.md#hearing.Channel)(\*values)                             | Which capture channel a segment came from.                                |
| [`SpeakerLabel`](_autosummary/hearing.html.md#hearing.SpeakerLabel)                                  |                                                                           |

### *class* hearing.Channel(\*values)

Bases: [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Enum`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/enum.html#enum.Enum)

Which capture channel a segment came from.

The channel *is* the “me vs them” signal, for free: `MIC` is the local
user, `SYSTEM` is everyone else (audio that came out of the speakers).
`MIXED` is a single-channel / unknown source.

### hearing.SpeakerLabel

alias of [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### *class* hearing.TimeSpan(start_ms, end_ms)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A half-open interval `[start_ms, end_ms)` in integer milliseconds.

Integer time, never float seconds — accumulation-safe and hashable.

```pycon
>>> TimeSpan(0, 1500).duration_ms
1500
```

#### *property* duration_ms *: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*

Length of the interval in milliseconds.

#### *classmethod* from_seconds(start, end)

Build a span from float seconds (e.g. from an STT engine).

* **Return type:**
  [`TimeSpan`](_autosummary/hearing.types.html.md#hearing.types.TimeSpan)

### *class* hearing.Transcript(segments=(), sample_rate=None, meta=dict())

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A finished transcript: an ordered collection of segments plus metadata.

Iterable and `len`-able, so it stands in for a `Sequence` of segments
wherever the architecture’s facades return “segments”. Adds convenience
accessors the CLI/agents need.

```pycon
>>> t = Transcript((TranscriptSegment("a", TimeSpan(0, 1000), speaker=ME),
...                  TranscriptSegment("b", TimeSpan(1000, 2000), speaker=THEM)))
>>> t.text
'a b'
>>> len(t)
2
>>> sorted(t.speakers)
['me', 'them']
```

#### *property* duration_ms *: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)*

End of the last segment, or 0 if empty.

#### formatted(, speakers=True, timestamps=True)

Render as a human-readable transcript, one line per segment.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

#### *property* speakers *: [set](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#set)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]*

The distinct speaker labels present (ignoring `None`).

#### *property* text *: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)*

All segment texts joined by a single space.

#### to_jsonable()

A plain `list[dict]` ready for `json.dumps` (segments only).

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]

#### with_meta(\*\*kw)

Return a copy with extra metadata merged in.

* **Return type:**
  [`Transcript`](_autosummary/hearing.types.html.md#hearing.types.Transcript)

### *class* hearing.TranscriptSegment(text, span, channel=Channel.MIXED, speaker=None, confidence=None, words=(), meta=dict())

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

The data spine — a standoff interval annotation over the audio.

Required fields are `text` and `span`. Everything else is optional
metadata that a concern *enriches*: STT sets `text`/`span`/
`confidence`; capture sets `channel`; diarization sets `speaker`.
Segments are frozen — enrich by copying (`with_speaker`/`with_channel`),
never mutate.

```pycon
>>> seg = TranscriptSegment("hello", TimeSpan(0, 500))
>>> seg.with_speaker(ME).speaker
'me'
>>> seg.text
'hello'
```

#### with_channel(channel)

Return a copy carrying a channel label (frozen -> copy, don’t mutate).

* **Return type:**
  [`TranscriptSegment`](_autosummary/hearing.types.html.md#hearing.types.TranscriptSegment)

#### with_speaker(speaker)

Return a copy carrying a speaker label (frozen -> copy, don’t mutate).

* **Return type:**
  [`TranscriptSegment`](_autosummary/hearing.types.html.md#hearing.types.TranscriptSegment)

### *class* hearing.Word(text, span, confidence=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Optional word-level timing (WhisperX / `word_timestamps=True`).

Lets an agent trigger on a keyword mid-utterance instead of waiting for the
end of a turn. Purely optional metadata on a [`TranscriptSegment`](_autosummary/hearing.html.md#hearing.TranscriptSegment).

### *async* hearing.live_transcribe(, source, engine=None, diarizer=None, agent=None, audio_queue_max=50, segment_queue_max=100)

Stream FINALIZED segments as a meeting unfolds (the live path).

Same components as [`transcribe()`](_autosummary/hearing.html.md#hearing.transcribe) — only the *source* (a streaming
[`CaptureSource`](_autosummary/hearing.interfaces.html.md#hearing.interfaces.CaptureSource) instead of a file) and the trigger
cadence (VAD utterance turn-ends instead of run-once) change. The
`STTEngine` and `AgentConsumer` interfaces are unchanged.

Each channel is demuxed onto its own bounded queue and driven through
`engine.stream_transcribe` as an independent async task, so a slow agent
never stalls capture (backpressure) and the channel “me vs them” label rides
every segment. Diarization defaults to the free channel trick; the agent’s
`on_segment` is fired fire-and-forget. Yields segments as utterances finalize.

See the `hearing-live-pipeline` skill.

### hearing.summarize(source, , agent=None, context=None, model=None, \*\*transcribe_kwargs)

Transcribe (if needed) then run an agent to produce meeting notes.

Accepts an audio source or an already-built [`Transcript`](_autosummary/hearing.html.md#hearing.Transcript). Builds the
default agent (Claude if available, else the offline extractive fallback)
when none is injected.

* **Return type:**
  [`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### hearing.transcribe(source, , engine=None, diarizer=None, agent=None, language=None, split=True, mic_channels=(0,), system_channels=(1,), record=None)

Transcribe an audio source to a [`Transcript`](_autosummary/hearing.types.html.md#hearing.types.Transcript).

The one-liner `transcribe("meeting.wav")` works with all defaults: the
default local engine (faster-whisper), automatic channel splitting when the
file is multi-channel, and the free “me vs them” channel-trick diarizer.

* **Parameters:**
  * **source** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path) | [`CaptureSource`](_autosummary/hearing.interfaces.html.md#hearing.interfaces.CaptureSource)) – a file path or any [`CaptureSource`](_autosummary/hearing.interfaces.html.md#hearing.interfaces.CaptureSource).
  * **engine** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`STTEngine`](_autosummary/hearing.interfaces.html.md#hearing.interfaces.STTEngine)]) – STT engine (default: faster-whisper). Inject any `STTEngine`.
  * **diarizer** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`Diarizer`](_autosummary/hearing.interfaces.html.md#hearing.interfaces.Diarizer)]) – speaker labeller. `None` -> the channel trick is applied
    automatically when channel info is present (mic=”me”, system=”them”).
    Inject a `PyannoteDiarizer` to separate individual remote speakers.
  * **agent** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`AgentConsumer`](_autosummary/hearing.interfaces.html.md#hearing.interfaces.AgentConsumer)]) – optional `AgentConsumer` run over the finished transcript
    (batch). Its output is stored under `transcript.meta['insight']`.
  * **language** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – force a language code (e.g. “en”); `None` = auto-detect.
  * **split** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – split mic/system channels when the source is multi-channel.
  * **system_channels** ([`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]) – column indices for the channel split.
  * **record** – optional `MutableMapping` store (e.g. a dol store) to persist
    the transcript JSON under key `"<source>.transcript.json"`.
* **Return type:**
  [`Transcript`](_autosummary/hearing.types.html.md#hearing.types.Transcript)
* **Returns:**
  A [`Transcript`](_autosummary/hearing.html.md#hearing.Transcript) (iterable/len-able, so it stands in for a sequence
  of segments). Segments carry text, span, channel, and speaker.

# _autosummary/hearing.interfaces.html.md

# hearing.interfaces

Facade Protocols for the four pipeline concerns.

Every engine/component is dependency-injected as one of these; the pipeline
depends only on these interfaces, never on a concrete engine. Implementers
satisfy them *structurally* (`typing.Protocol`) — they do not subclass.

This is the contract the `hearing-architecture` skill defines and that every
other `hearing-*` concern implements against.

### Classes

| [`AgentConsumer`](_autosummary/hearing.interfaces.html.md#hearing.interfaces.AgentConsumer)(\*args, \*\*kwargs)   | Consumes the (labeled) transcript stream and does things.          |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`CaptureSource`](_autosummary/hearing.interfaces.html.md#hearing.interfaces.CaptureSource)(\*args, \*\*kwargs)   | Audio source — the ONLY thing that differs between batch and live. |
| [`Diarizer`](_autosummary/hearing.interfaces.html.md#hearing.interfaces.Diarizer)(\*args, \*\*kwargs)        | Labels who spoke — enriches segments with `.speaker`.              |
| [`STTEngine`](_autosummary/hearing.interfaces.html.md#hearing.interfaces.STTEngine)(\*args, \*\*kwargs)       | Speech-to-text.                                                    |

### *class* hearing.interfaces.AgentConsumer(\*args, \*\*kwargs)

Bases: [`Protocol`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Protocol)

Consumes the (labeled) transcript stream and does things.

Running notes, suggested questions, RAG over related docs, post-meeting
summaries. Defaults to Claude but stays pluggable (see the `claude-api`
skill for model ids / pricing / tool use).

#### *async* on_segment(segment)

Called per finalized segment (live). Return an optional insight.

* **Return type:**
  [`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

#### *async* on_window(window)

Called on a window/turn or the whole transcript (batch).

Return an optional insight (summary, action items, a suggested
question, a surfaced document, …).

* **Return type:**
  [`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### *class* hearing.interfaces.CaptureSource(\*args, \*\*kwargs)

Bases: [`Protocol`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Protocol)

Audio source — the ONLY thing that differs between batch and live.

Yields `(channel, frames)` so mic and system audio stay on separate
channels all the way down. A batch implementation reads a file; a live
implementation reads a device/tap.

#### astream()

Live / async: yield `(channel, frames)` blocks until stopped.

* **Return type:**
  [`AsyncIterator`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.AsyncIterator)[[`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`Channel`](_autosummary/hearing.types.html.md#hearing.types.Channel), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]]

#### frames()

Batch / sync: yield `(channel, frames[n_samples])` blocks to EOF.

* **Return type:**
  [`Iterator`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Iterator)[[`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`Channel`](_autosummary/hearing.types.html.md#hearing.types.Channel), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]]

### *class* hearing.interfaces.Diarizer(\*args, \*\*kwargs)

Bases: [`Protocol`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Protocol)

Labels who spoke — enriches segments with `.speaker`.

May use the audio (pyannote) or just the channel (the channel trick).
Identity resolution (`spk_0` -> `"Alice"`) is an optional further step
behind the same interface.

#### assign_speakers(segments, , audio=None, sample_rate=None)

Yield segments with `.speaker` populated (enrich-by-copy).

* **Return type:**
  [`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Iterable)[[`TranscriptSegment`](_autosummary/hearing.types.html.md#hearing.types.TranscriptSegment)]

### *class* hearing.interfaces.STTEngine(\*args, \*\*kwargs)

Bases: [`Protocol`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Protocol)

Speech-to-text.

`transcribe` is the batch one-liner; `stream_transcribe` is the live
variant. Both yield [`TranscriptSegment`](_autosummary/hearing.types.html.md#hearing.types.TranscriptSegment) — same shape,
same spine. The rest of the architecture never names a concrete engine.

#### *async* stream_transcribe(frames, , sample_rate)

Live: yield interim then finalized segments as audio arrives.

Mark interim vs final via `meta` (e.g. `meta['final']`). See the
`hearing-live-pipeline` skill — this is the milestone-2 entry point.

* **Return type:**
  [`AsyncIterator`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.AsyncIterator)[[`TranscriptSegment`](_autosummary/hearing.types.html.md#hearing.types.TranscriptSegment)]

#### transcribe(audio, , sample_rate, language=None)

Batch: whole clip in (float32 mono ndarray), segments out.

* **Return type:**
  [`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[`TranscriptSegment`](_autosummary/hearing.types.html.md#hearing.types.TranscriptSegment)]


# _autosummary/hearing.pipeline.html.md

# hearing.pipeline

Pipeline assembly — compose the four concerns by dependency injection.

This is where progressive disclosure lives: `transcribe("meeting.wav")` is a
one-liner with smart defaults, while the engine, diarizer, agent, channel
routing, and persistence are all optional keyword-only arguments. The same
shape powers the live path (`live_transcribe`); only the *source* and the
*trigger cadence* differ (milestone 2).

See the `hearing-architecture` skill — this module is the thin orchestrator it
describes; swapping any one component touches only the assembly call.

### Functions

| [`live_transcribe`](_autosummary/hearing.pipeline.html.md#hearing.pipeline.live_transcribe)(\*, source[, engine, ...])      | Stream FINALIZED segments as a meeting unfolds (the live path).                                                       |

| [`summarize`](_autosummary/hearing.pipeline.html.md#hearing.pipeline.summarize)(source, \*[, agent, context, model])  | Transcribe (if needed) then run an agent to produce meeting notes.                                                    |
| [`transcribe`](_autosummary/hearing.pipeline.html.md#hearing.pipeline.transcribe)(source, \*[, engine, diarizer, ...]) | Transcribe an audio source to a [`Transcript`](_autosummary/hearing.types.html.md#hearing.types.Transcript). |

cadence (VAD utterance turn-ends instead of run-once) change. The

Each channel is demuxed onto its own bounded queue and driven through

# _autosummary/hearing.storage.html.md

# hearing.storage

Transcript persistence via key-value stores (python-storage / `dol`).

A transcript is standoff annotation data — persist the *whole* transcript (not
just a rolling window) so post-meeting agents see everything (see the
`hearing-agents` and `annotation-systems` skills). [`MeetingStore`](_autosummary/hearing.storage.html.md#hearing.storage.MeetingStore)
saves/loads transcripts as JSON keyed by meeting id, over any
`MutableMapping` — a plain dict (tests), a `dol` store (e.g. `TextFiles`),
or the dependency-free filesystem fallback here.

### Functions

| [`get_store`](_autosummary/hearing.storage.html.md#hearing.storage.get_store)([path])              | Return a string-valued `MutableMapping` for transcripts.                                                      |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`transcript_from_json`](_autosummary/hearing.storage.html.md#hearing.storage.transcript_from_json)(s)        | Reconstruct a `Transcript` from [`transcript_to_json()`](_autosummary/hearing.storage.html.md#hearing.storage.transcript_to_json) output. |
| [`transcript_to_json`](_autosummary/hearing.storage.html.md#hearing.storage.transcript_to_json)(transcript) | Serialize a `Transcript` to a JSON string (round-trippable).                                                  |

### Classes

| [`MeetingStore`](_autosummary/hearing.storage.html.md#hearing.storage.MeetingStore)([store])   | Save/load transcripts keyed by meeting id, over any text MutableMapping.   |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### *class* hearing.storage.MeetingStore(store=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Save/load transcripts keyed by meeting id, over any text MutableMapping.

```pycon
>>> store = MeetingStore({})                       # in-memory
>>> from hearing.types import Transcript, TranscriptSegment, TimeSpan
>>> _ = store.save("m1", Transcript([TranscriptSegment("hi", TimeSpan(0, 500))]))
>>> store.load("m1").text
'hi'
>>> list(store)
['m1']
```

#### load(meeting_id)

Load the transcript stored under `meeting_id`.

* **Return type:**
  [`Transcript`](_autosummary/hearing.types.html.md#hearing.types.Transcript)

#### meeting_ids()

Sorted ids of stored meetings.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

#### save(meeting_id, transcript)

Persist `transcript` under `meeting_id`; return the storage key.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### hearing.storage.get_store(path=None)

Return a string-valued `MutableMapping` for transcripts.

`None` -> an in-memory dict. A path -> a `dol.TextFiles` store if `dol`
is installed (`pip install 'hearing[storage]'`), else the dependency-free
`_FileTextStore` over that directory.

* **Return type:**
  [`MutableMapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping)

### hearing.storage.transcript_from_json(s)

Reconstruct a `Transcript` from [`transcript_to_json()`](_autosummary/hearing.storage.html.md#hearing.storage.transcript_to_json) output.

* **Return type:**
  [`Transcript`](_autosummary/hearing.types.html.md#hearing.types.Transcript)

### hearing.storage.transcript_to_json(transcript)

Serialize a `Transcript` to a JSON string (round-trippable).

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)


# _autosummary/hearing.stt.html.md

# hearing.stt

Speech-to-text for hearing — now backed by the scribed transcription façade.

hearing no longer implements its own STT engines. It consumes **scribed** (one
façade over many engines) and adapts scribed’s normalized `Transcript`/`Segment`
spine to hearing’s [`TranscriptSegment`](_autosummary/hearing.types.html.md#hearing.types.TranscriptSegment) data model. The rest of
the architecture still sees only the [`STTEngine`](_autosummary/hearing.interfaces.html.md#hearing.interfaces.STTEngine) Protocol:
`transcribe(audio) -> segments` and `stream_transcribe(frames) -> segments`.

The default engine is scribed’s faster-whisper backend (local, fast). Swap engines by
changing the scribed `backend=` (e.g. `"openai"`) — nothing downstream changes.
See scribed’s `scribed-choose-backend` skill for the full engine landscape, pricing,
and the local-vs-cloud decision.

Engines by friendly name ([`ENGINE_ALIASES`](_autosummary/hearing.stt.html.md#hearing.stt.ENGINE_ALIASES), used by [`get_engine()`](_autosummary/hearing.stt.html.md#hearing.stt.get_engine) and the
CLI’s `--engine`):

- `whisper` — faster-whisper, local, any CPU/GPU (default; `hearing[whisper]`)
- `openai` — OpenAI transcription API (`hearing[openai]`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`)
- `deepgram` — Deepgram Nova-3 (`hearing[deepgram]`, `DEEPGRAM_API_KEY`)
- `mlx` / `parakeet` — Whisper / Parakeet-TDT on Apple Silicon (`hearing[mlx]`)
- `whisperx` — WhisperX, aligned words + optional diarization (`hearing[whisperx]`)

The last three are scribed backends that hearing itself contributes
([`hearing.backends`](_autosummary/hearing.backends.html.md#module-hearing.backends)); they are registered with scribed on first use.

### Module Attributes

| [`DEFAULT_BACKEND`](_autosummary/hearing.stt.html.md#hearing.stt.DEFAULT_BACKEND)        | Default scribed backend id for local transcription.                             |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`ENGINE_ALIASES`](_autosummary/hearing.stt.html.md#hearing.stt.ENGINE_ALIASES)         | Friendly engine name -> scribed backend id (the SSOT for `get_engine`/the CLI). |
| [`WHISPER_SIZED_BACKENDS`](_autosummary/hearing.stt.html.md#hearing.stt.WHISPER_SIZED_BACKENDS) | Backends whose `model` accepts a bare whisper size ("base", "small", ...).      |
| [`ENGINE_NAMES`](_autosummary/hearing.stt.html.md#hearing.stt.ENGINE_NAMES)           | Engine names shown in help and error messages (one per backend).                |

### Functions

| [`DeepgramSTT`](_autosummary/hearing.stt.html.md#hearing.stt.DeepgramSTT)(\*[, model])           | Deepgram (cloud) engine — Nova-3 by default; `model="nova-2"` etc.                                                        |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`FasterWhisperSTT`](_autosummary/hearing.stt.html.md#hearing.stt.FasterWhisperSTT)(\*[, model_size]) | Backward-compatible constructor for the local engine (returns a `ScribedSTT`).                                            |
| [`MLXSTT`](_autosummary/hearing.stt.html.md#hearing.stt.MLXSTT)(\*[, model, mlx_backend])   | Apple-Silicon (MLX) engine: mlx-whisper by default, or `mlx_backend="parakeet-mlx"`.                                      |
| [`OpenAISTT`](_autosummary/hearing.stt.html.md#hearing.stt.OpenAISTT)(\*\*kwargs)              | Backward-compatible constructor for the OpenAI engine (returns a `ScribedSTT`).                                           |
| [`WhisperXSTT`](_autosummary/hearing.stt.html.md#hearing.stt.WhisperXSTT)(\*[, model, diarize])  | WhisperX engine: aligned word timestamps, plus pyannote speakers if `diarize`.                                            |
| [`default_engine`](_autosummary/hearing.stt.html.md#hearing.stt.default_engine)(\*\*kwargs)         | Return the project's default STT engine (scribed faster-whisper).                                                         |
| [`get_engine`](_autosummary/hearing.stt.html.md#hearing.stt.get_engine)([name])                 | Build a scribed-backed STT engine by friendly name (see [`ENGINE_ALIASES`](_autosummary/hearing.stt.html.md#hearing.stt.ENGINE_ALIASES)). |

### Classes

| [`ScribedSTT`](_autosummary/hearing.stt.html.md#hearing.stt.ScribedSTT)([backend, model_size, language, ...])   | An `STTEngine` backed by scribed — the single engine hearing now uses.   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|

### hearing.stt.DEFAULT_BACKEND *: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)* *= 'faster-whisper'*

Deepgram (cloud) engine — Nova-3 by default; `model="nova-2"` etc. swaps it.

Batch goes to Deepgram’s pre-recorded REST API (via scribed’s deepgram backend);
the live path is scribed’s VAD-segmented stream over that batch call. Needs
`pip install 'hearing[deepgram]'` and `DEEPGRAM_API_KEY`.

Backward-compatible constructor for the local engine (returns a `ScribedSTT`).

Apple-Silicon (MLX) engine: mlx-whisper by default, or `mlx_backend="parakeet-mlx"`.

`model` is a Hugging Face repo id or (mlx-whisper) a bare Whisper size such as
